title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-04-05
lineage: SBD > Rm (7 inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) > DAT > Sonic Solutions > CD > EAC > Samplitude > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear Charlie Miller soundboard captures a high‑energy 1969 Avalon show highlighted by a smoking Mountains/Dark Star segue and monster Alligator/Eleven jams.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑preserved soundboard capture with excellent clarity (only the faint hiss typical of ’69 tapes). The performance is an ecstatic snapshot of the Dead at their psychedelic peak – tight acoustic openings morph into electric fire, with standout moments like Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star, Alligator, The Eleven and Cryptical Envelopment. Energy stays high throughout, despite a few weaker spots such as Hard To Handle.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews (majority 5‑star) praise both the musical performance and the sound quality; only a handful of minor criticisms appear, yielding a rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp mix with minimal tape hiss; reviewers note “great sound”, “clean quality”, and “excellent recording”. A few mention a slight hiss but no drop‑outs or major flaws.

standout_songs: Mountains of the Moon → Dark Star
show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic opener (Dupree’s, Mountains of the Moon) flows into electric psychedelia; unique segues like Cryptical > Eleven and a surprising William‑Tell → Lovelight cut add intrigue. The set builds to a high‑octane second half with Alligator, The Other One suite and a long Feedback jam.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for fiery guitar tone, aggressive Dark Star solo, slide work on Hard To Handle (mixed), and vocal presence; described as “on fire” and “masterful”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “bombs” on Alligator, strong bass throughout, and tight interplay with the dual drummers.
band_member_comments.Bob: Early‑stage rhythm guitar/voice noted; some reviewers mention vocal cracks on Cosmic Charlie but also acknowledge his developing style.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s carousel‑like piano on Dupree’s is highlighted; overall keyboards provide atmospheric depth.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and Mickey described as a single creature with six arms, delivering tight, powerful rhythms especially during The Eleven and Alligator.
